title: Building Your Personal AI Stack
description: Design a set of AI tools and workflows tailored to your work, life, and goals — without falling into tool overload.

data.text: By this point in the course you've encountered many AI tools. The challenge now is deciding which ones to actually use, together, in a coherent way. This is your personal AI stack.
A framework for building your stack

items: List your top 5 most time-consuming, repeated tasks at work
Identify which tasks involve writing, research, analysis, or coordination
Match each task category to the best AI tool for it
Commit to 2-3 tools maximum for 90 days — resist adding more
Review and adjust after 90 days based on what you actually used

data.text: Think in stack layers, not random apps

A durable personal AI stack usually has four layers: a conversation layer (thinking and drafting), a research layer (verification and source discovery), a creation layer (documents, visuals, code, or slides), and an operations layer (storage, notes, and repeatable templates). When a tool clearly serves one layer, decisions become simpler and you avoid overlapping subscriptions.

data.text: How to evaluate a tool before adding it

rows: Does it improve a repeated weekly task?
Saves meaningful time in a real task
Are outputs clearly better than current baseline?
Does quality stay consistent across similar prompts?
Can it connect with your existing notes/files/workspace?
Is value higher than subscription and switching cost?

data.title: Avoid tool overload
data.text: The biggest mistake is collecting tools instead of building habits. Two tools you use daily are worth more than twenty you have accounts for.

data.title: Beware false productivity
data.text: A new tool can feel fast while quietly increasing review time. Track end-to-end completion time and quality, not just draft speed. If a tool creates extra verification work, your total workflow may be slower.

rows: Stabilize 2 core workflows with one primary tool
Consolidate stack and remove low-value tools
Clear weekly usage pattern plus lower tool sprawl

items.text: Am I using each tool at least once a week?
Is there a tool I could replace with one I already have?
Have any of my tools improved enough to reconsider my setup?
Am I paying for tools I no longer use?

data.title: Your AI stack principles
points: Start minimal: 2-3 tools max for 90 days
Choose by task, not by news coverage
Depth beats breadth — master one tool before adding another
Review quarterly and cut what you do not use
